# Contributing to RAiNBOW_Hello-World

Thanks for helping make the bar more rainbow.

## The one rule that matters

**Never change a byte in `hello/core/` by hand.** Those files are regenerated by
CI. `scripts/generate_all_hello.py` writes them and `scripts/balance_bytes.py`
pads every one of them to exactly 2048 bytes so each language gets an identical
slice of the bar. Editing them by hand produces a commit that CI will silently
revert.

If a core file is wrong, fix the generator, not the output.

## Getting set up

```bash
git clone https://github.com/quxianp/RAiNBOW_Hello-World.git
cd RAiNBOW_Hello-World

# Optional: figlet, toilet, lolcat, ffmpeg, ttyd. Everything degrades gracefully.
./install_deps.sh

# Python 3.10+ with PyYAML, requests, beautifulsoup4, pillow, matplotlib.
python -m pip install pyyaml requests beautifulsoup4 pillow matplotlib
```

## Before you push

```bash
python scripts/verify_languages.py     # 19 acceptance checks
python scripts/validate_delivery.py    # workflow, layout, generators, exec bits
python scripts/balance_bytes.py        # must be idempotent: zero drift
bash run.sh                            # must exit 0
```

`validate_delivery.py` is the one that catches most mistakes: it runs the README
generators, compiles every script, and fails if `run.sh` stops passing the
animation flags.

## Adding a language

1. If Linguist already colours it, it is almost certainly already in
   `hello/core/`. Check `config/core-langs.txt` first.
2. If it is missing, add it to the built-in fallback groups in
   `scripts/fetch_languages.py`, then re-run the pipeline:

   ```bash
   python scripts/fetch_languages.py
   python scripts/merge_language_sources.py
   python scripts/select_rainbow_langs.py
   python scripts/generate_all_hello.py
   python scripts/balance_bytes.py
   python scripts/verify_languages.py
   ```

3. Languages Linguist gives **no colour** cannot go on a colour bar. COBOL is
   the famous example. They belong in `hello/full/`, which is vendored.

## Working on the demo

The recording is a VHS tape. `demo.tape` drives it; `scripts/record_demo.sh`
runs VHS and then transcodes with ffmpeg.

```bash
vhs demo.tape                          # assets/hello-world.gif
bash scripts/record_demo.sh            # gif + mp4, with GIF optimisation
python scripts/generate_hero_banner.py # banner, counts read from the repo
python scripts/render_github_bar.py    # the 631-language bar image
```

`run.sh` has motion settings (`--motion`, `--fast`) so you can iterate on one
phase without re-rendering everything.

## Commit messages

Short imperative subject, explain *why* in the body. If your commit triggers CI,
add `[skip ci]` to the subject — the bot's own asset commits do this, and it is
what stops the pipeline from looping.

## Reporting a problem

Open an issue with the command you ran and its output. If the language bar looks
wrong, `python scripts/audit_repo.py` prints a health report that is usually
enough to identify the cause.
